page.layout: One printed page with a running head at top and page number at top right; main text in two columns of unequal width on the right side; on the left, a narrow strip of text from a facing page (cropped, partly cut by the gutter) lies outside the text block as margin text. Reading order: main text right page top to bottom; the left strip is a margin of the facing page and is transcribed as notes.

main_text.l: 18 Forma tria habet officia, 1. Deter-
minate rem constituere, unde forma voca-
tur. 2. Effentialiter eam distinguere, un-
de appellatur differentia. 3. Efficere ope-
rationes & actiones quarum est principi-
um, unde actus nominatur.
19 Finis exurgit ex conjunctione m-
ateriæ & formæ,& est illa bonitas vel per-
fectio rei qua elt ad operationem & usum apta.
20 Bonitas hæc in efficientis intentio-
ne,est adjuvans causa; ufus ad quem ten-
dit, est effectum; res vel persona cui inser-
vit in usu,est objectum:ad hæc tamen om-
nia propter affinitatem, finis nomen solet
applicari:bonitas vel aptitudo ad usum est
proprie finalis causa;appetitio ejus impel-
lens efficientem,est finis intentionis; usus
est secundarius finis cujus; res vel persona
ad quam petat est finis cui.& in his om-
nibus generibus,unus aliquando finis operis
dicitur;& alius operantis: sed scopus o-
perantis à natura operis alienus, per ac-
cidens, tantum finis dicitur operationis.
21 Quamvis causæ distinctæ sint es-
sentia & definitione, res tamen quæ
vi causarum fit unicam habet naturam, quæ
licet arguatur à singulis causis, tamen ab
efficiente ut à principio quod primam vim
exerit

page.notes: Left strip is the cropped facing page (partly illegible, Latin and Italian fragments of text such as "unde", "tanquam", "dicitur"); not transcribed in full because it is cut off by the gutter and too fragmentary to read reliably. The main text's last line is continued on the next page as "exerit" printed at the right.
